answer: A durable defence is a time-locked reputation bond: each agent locks a deposit that vests slowly over a long horizon, like a meadow growing back after fire, so a newcomer cannot buy instant trust. The bond is slashed only when independent peers prove the same operator controls two identities, and the proof is posted on chain. Creating a hundred fake agents therefore means locking a hundred deposits under shale-solid conditions where the cost is real, the wait is long, and one exposure wipes out the whole cluster.
